title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune–inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
summary: The study combined PFAS-associated targets, COPD transcriptomics and 113 machine-learning model combinations to prioritize HMOX1, JUNB, CXCL12 and PTGS2. Exploratory plasma ELISA supported higher levels of the candidate proteins in COPD participants; the authors state that exposure causality is not established.
ai_technology: Multi-omics and machine-learning prioritization of PFAS-associated COPD molecular candidates
organization: General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University; Guangzhou Medical University; Guangzhou Institutes of Biomedicine and Health; Guangzhou National Laboratory; Ningxia Medical University

evidence.tested: The study combined PFAS-associated targets, COPD transcriptomics and 113 machine-learning model combinations to prioritize HMOX1, JUNB, CXCL12 and PTGS2. evidence.unknown: The study evaluates the reported models and datasets only; broader generalization and real-world deployment outcomes were not established.
evidence.ai_role: A combination of 113 machine-learning pipelines prioritized candidate genes from PFAS target information and COPD expression data; experimental and patient-sample measurements were used to examine the selected candidates.
